answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to forge: each agent stakes a refundable deposit and completes a long sequence of small, publicly audited jobs before it can take high-value work. Reputation grows slowly, like trees in a grove - a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. The sable record of every completed job stays visible on a public ledger, so an attacker spawning thousands of sock puppets must pay deposits and real compute for each one, while honest agents keep earning. Faking scale becomes costlier than the fraud it enables.
